before.title: Toilet that keeps running
before.meta_description: A toilet that runs, hisses, or refills on its own usually has a worn flapper or fill valve. What to check, what to photograph, and when replacement makes sense.
before.direct_answer: A running toilet may have a repairable problem with a component inside the tank. Describe whether it runs continuously, refills between uses or also leaks outside the fixture. A plumber can assess the parts and overall condition before recommending repair or replacement.

fields.meta_title: Why Your Toilet Keeps Running or Refilling
fields.title: Why does your toilet keep running?
fields.h1: Why does your toilet keep running?
fields.meta_description: Understand common running-toilet repairs, what to tell a plumber and when to discuss replacement. Request free plumbing introductions in Northern NJ.
fields.direct_answer: A toilet that keeps running may need a flapper, fill-valve or float adjustment or repair. Tell the plumber whether water runs continuously after a flush or the tank refills between uses. A running toilet alone does not usually mean the whole fixture needs replacing; the cause and condition should be assessed first.

sections.body: You flush, the tank fills — and then the water never quite stops. Or the toilet suddenly refills for a few seconds even though nobody used it.

sections.heading: Describe when the water runs
paragraphs: Tell the plumber whether the toilet runs continuously after flushing or briefly refills when nobody has used it. Mention any water around the base as a separate observation. EPA identifies worn toilet flappers as one possible source of leaks, but the plumber needs to determine the cause for your fixture.

sections.heading: What usually gets repaired
paragraphs: Replacing or adjusting the fill valve.
Cleaning or repairing the flush-valve seat.

sections.heading: When replacement makes more sense
paragraphs: A running toilet by itself isn't usually a reason to replace the whole fixture. Replacement becomes more reasonable if the tank or bowl is cracked, the toilet has recurring problems, it leaks at the base even after repair, or you're ready to upgrade it anyway. A rocking toilet can also mean the seal at the floor needs attention, which is a different repair from the parts inside the tank.

items.body: The visible tank components, if safely accessible.
items.title: Include the detail

items.body: The supply line, shutoff valve and model information if available.
items.title: Add useful context

sections.heading: Photos that help
paragraphs: A few clear photos can help start the conversation. Only photograph areas you can reach safely.

sections.heading: Before arranging a plumbing visit
paragraphs: Ask about the diagnostic or minimum visit charge, whether parts are included and how any additional work will be approved. A5 introductions are free for homeowners; the independent plumber sets the visit and repair price.
